reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only states that pits initiate preferentially at grain boundaries in the Cantor alloy, especially in fine-grained, high-stress specimens, and does not address repassivation kinetics, film repair rates, or tribo-corrosion. The key premises about grain boundaries enhancing rapid film repair and governing the coupled wear-corrosion response are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi act as active sites for rapid oxide/passive film repair.
Fine-grained microstructures (high grain boundary density) enhance repassivation kinetics.
Coarse-grained microstructures (low grain boundary density) exhibit slower passive film reformation.
Slower repassivation in coarse-grained alloys leads to prolonged exposure and enhanced localized corrosion.
Under identical wear, fine-grained alloys will show similar mechanical wear but lower corrosion than coarse-grained alloys.
